h1: Whisky in the duty free channel
title: Whisky in the Duty Free Channel | Craft Beer School
desc: How whisky is sold in duty free and travel retail: who buys, why packs differ, how pricing and allowances work and what it means for the brand team.
teaser: Duty free shops sell whisky to people in a hurry with a boarding pass in their hand. That changes almost everything.
standfirst: Travel retail is a small channel by volume with an outsized role in how whisky brands launch, price and present themselves. This guide explains how it works for the teams who plan, price and report it.
sections:
Duty free shops sell goods to international travellers without the local excise and import duties that a domestic shop must charge. The logic is that the traveller is taking the goods out of the country, or bringing them in within a personal allowance. The industry calls the wider channel travel retail, which also covers airline sales, border shops and cruise ships.

For whisky the duty is a large part of the shelf price in most markets. Take it away and a bottle can sit well below its domestic price. That gap is the whole reason the channel exists. It shapes everything below.

The duty free shopper is not the same as the domestic shopper. They are time pressed, often buying a gift and comparing prices against what they know from home. Many buy whisky they would not pick up in a local shop because it is a treat, a gift for family or simply cheaper here.

That makes travel retail a showcase. Brands use it to launch new expressions, test premium packs and reach drinkers from many countries in one place. A traveller from Bengaluru may meet a whisky in Dubai before it is sold in Karnataka.

Travel retail packs often differ from domestic packs. One litre bottles are common in the channel, where domestic Indian whisky is usually sold in 750, 375 and 180 ml. Gift tins, twin packs and travel exclusive expressions (whiskies sold only in duty free) are standard tools.

For the production team, a travel exclusive is a real planning task. It needs its own liquid, often a particular cask finish or age, its own label artwork and its own bottling run. A one litre bottle at 40% ABV holds 0.4 litres of pure alcohol against 0.3 for a 750 ml bottle at the same strength, so stock planning has to work in litres of alcohol rather than bottles. Our guide to how limited edition whiskies are planned covers the same stock logic.
Allowances limit what a traveller can carry

Arriving passengers can bring in a limited quantity of alcohol without paying duty. The limit is set by each country's customs rules, usually in litres per adult. It changes from time to time. Anything above it attracts duty at the border.

For the brand team this matters because the allowance caps the basket. A traveller with room for two litres chooses carefully, which favours larger packs and recognisable brands. Always check the current customs baggage rules in each country before planning a promotion around them.

Indian international airports have duty free shops for arriving passengers as well as departing ones. That puts the domestic brand team and the travel retail team in the same terminal, selling to the same returning traveller, sometimes with different packs and prices. Agree between the two teams which expressions belong where before the traveller notices the overlap for you.

Duty free prices are set with an eye on domestic prices in the traveller's home market. If a whisky is far cheaper in a duty free shop than at home, travellers stock up. If it is barely cheaper, they skip it. Brands also watch for travel retail stock leaking into domestic markets, which undercuts local distributors and confuses price positioning.

Indian rules on stock bonded for duty free sale and its movement to airport shops are handled under customs and state excise procedures that vary and change. Teams should check the current notification and take advice before setting up supply.
How travel retail shows up in the data

Travel retail usually sits in its own reporting line, separate from domestic states. Sales are often recorded by the shop operator and shared with the brand on a schedule, priced in a different currency and sometimes in different pack sizes. Footfall at the airport drives the channel, so passenger numbers are a common explanatory variable in forecasts.

Do not add travel retail cases to domestic cases without converting to a common unit. Nine litre equivalent cases or litres of pure alcohol both work. Mixing one litre bottles with 750 ml bottles as if they were the same case is a classic dashboard error.

Pick one whisky in your portfolio that is sold in travel retail. Compare its duty free price with its domestic price in the same currency, then note the pack size of each. If the duty free pack is a litre, convert both to price per litre of pure alcohol. That single number tells you whether the channel is a showcase, a bargain or a leak.
faqs: Travel retail is the sale of goods to international travellers in airports, on flights, at border shops and on ships, usually without local excise and import duties.
Why are duty free whisky bottles often one litre?
One litre is a common travel retail pack size. Domestic Indian whisky is usually sold in 750, 375 and 180 ml bottles.
How much whisky can a traveller bring into India duty free?
Customs baggage rules set a personal allowance in litres per adult and they change over time. Check the current rules before travelling or planning a promotion.
